clue.text: An eye for a drink

explanation.surface: Someone with a keen talent for spotting a good tipple.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pubs the device that dispenses a fixed measure of spirits from an inverted bottle has the same name as a jocular word for an eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The bar measure fitted to a spirit bottle shares its name with the word meaning relating to vision.

clue.text: A group often described as vicious

explanation.surface: A gang with a reputation for nastiness.
explanation.definitionFit: A circle is a set of people sharing an interest, and a vicious circle is the familiar phrase for a self-feeding bad cycle.

clue.text: General plans for great changes in the pig-pen

indicators.note: in says the reworked letters sit inside the word for the pig-pen

parts.note: a pig-pen is a sty

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of great are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer plans big alterations to where the pigs live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' turns GREAT into RATEG, and 'in' puts that inside STY, between ST and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategy is an overall plan of action, the kind a general draws up.

clue.text: One more metamorphosis on earth

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a complete transformation, so the letters of on earth are rearranged

explanation.surface: Yet another transformation taking place on the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'metamorphosis' reshuffles the seven letters of ON EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means an additional one, a further example of the same kind.

clue.text: Used to speak highly of latest fashion

indicators.note: fashion as a verb means to shape, so the letters of of latest are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone praised the newest trend in clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' looks like a noun after 'latest' but is a verb telling us to rearrange OF LATEST. 'Speak highly' sounds like praise but means a high-pitched voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A falsetto is the artificially high register a male singer or speaker can adopt.

clue.text: Aunt Mabel, when wild, can't be controlled!

indicators.note: when wild says the letters of the name Aunt Mabel are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A relative called Mabel becomes unmanageable when she goes wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when wild' rearranges the nine letters of AUNT MABEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something untamable cannot be brought under control or domesticated.

clue.text: Fling it up, wildly cheering

indicators.note: wildly signals the letters of fling it up are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone throws something into the air while cheering wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges the letters of FLING IT UP.
explanation.definitionFit: Uplifting describes something that raises the spirits, as a cheering event does.

clue.text: Bath's sex appeal girl

parts.note: Una is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman from the city of Bath has plenty of allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bath' at the start looks like the English spa city; it is just a bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A sauna is a steam bath, a room heated for sweating.

clue.text: Big lake up country

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the word for the country is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for Ireland

explanation.surface: There is a large lake further north in the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses EIRE in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America.

clue.text: A machine to tune with skill

parts.note: an air is a tune
craft is skill

explanation.surface: A device for tuning instruments expertly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'with' just join the pieces; the machine is a flying one.
explanation.definitionFit: An aeroplane or helicopter is a flying machine.

clue.text: Car's crashed a learner-a culpable character

indicators.note: crashed says the letters are smashed up and rearranged

parts.note: the word car with its s
L is the learner sign on a car

explanation.surface: A learner driver has crashed the car and is to blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' rearranges CARS, A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a rogue or scamp, someone at fault for mischief.

clue.text: Said to be top dog

indicators.note: said to be signals that the word heard is spelt differently

parts.note: the peak is the top

explanation.surface: Rumour has it that this one is the champion hound.
explanation.walkthrough: A peke is short for Pekingese, a small dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Peke is the short name for the Pekingese breed of toy dog.

clue.text: Final change of venue at Leatherhead

indicators.note: change of says the letters of venue at are rearranged

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of leather is L

explanation.surface: A last-minute switch of location to the Surrey town of Leatherhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Leatherhead is a town in Surrey, but here it is the head of 'Leather'. 'change of' rearranges VENUE AT into EVENTUA.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual means coming at the end, ultimate.

clue.text: Turned out awkward without an instructor

indicators.note: awkward suggests clumsy disorder, so the letters of turned out are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone proved clumsy because nobody taught them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges TURNED OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Untutored means never having been taught, lacking formal teaching.

clue.text: Not many can provide a word of opposite meaning

indicators.note: can provide hints that the letters of not many can be rearranged into something new

explanation.surface: Few people can supply a word meaning the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can provide' rearranges NOT MANY.
explanation.definitionFit: An antonym is a word with the contrary sense, as hot is to cold.

clue.text: Brunettes not admitted? That's justifiable

explanation.surface: Excluding dark-haired people is defended as reasonable.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is a door policy admitting only blondes; the phrase also means reasonable.
explanation.definitionFit: Admitting just blondes is a fair-haired-only policy, and the phrase also means simply just or reasonable.

clue.text: Base for soldier in retreat, one of rank

indicators.note: in retreat says the word for the soldier goes backwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
a noble is a person of high rank

explanation.surface: A military base for a retreating soldier, an officer of rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a military camp; it means low or dishonourable.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignoble means dishonourable or mean, low in character.

clue.text: Boy admits disappearance of pocket dictionary

indicators.note: admits says the boy's name lets the other word inside it

parts.note: Gary is a boy's name
a loss is a disappearance

explanation.surface: A lad confesses that his small dictionary has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' looks like confesses; it puts LOSS inside GARY.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is a short list of terms with meanings, a small dictionary.

clue.text: Darting around, buying and selling

indicators.note: around signals the letters of darting are moved about

explanation.surface: Dashing about the market doing business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' rearranges DARTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Trading is commerce, the exchange of goods for money.

clue.text: Worn after rowing?

parts.note: a garment one might put on after exercise, but the question mark invites reading it as what comes after pulling an oar

explanation.surface: A garment put on after a session on the river.
explanation.walkthrough: To row is to pull, so when the pulling is over you have the jumper's name; a jumper is a knitted sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitted jumper is pulled on over the head, and its name also reads as rowing finished.

clue.text: It turns to face the blow

definitions.text: It turns to face the blow

parts.words: It turns to face the blow
parts.note: sounds like a boxer squaring up to a punch, but the blow is the wind

explanation.surface: A fighter who turns to meet a punch head on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blow' suggests a punch but means the wind, which a weathercock swings to point into.
explanation.definitionFit: A weathercock pivots on its spindle to point into the wind.

clue.text: Boozy group return to hold a wild party

indicators.note: return says the hidden letters are read backwards
to hold says the letters are held inside the words boozy group

explanation.surface: Drunken revellers head back to throw a riotous bash.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'hold', but the answer is a noun and 'to hold' is the hiding signal: YGRO spans 'BoozY GROup', and 'return' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a riotous drunken celebration, a debauched party.

clue.text: Oil found near Albania, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that a word is identified by its sound

parts.note: Greece is the country bordering Albania to the south

explanation.surface: Oil reserves discovered close to Albania, reportedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oil' as a verb or noun means lubricate or lubricant.
explanation.definitionFit: Grease is a thick oily lubricant.

clue.text: Sunbathed, topless, as requested

indicators.note: topless says the first letter is removed from the word for sunbathed

parts.note: to bask is to lie in the sun

explanation.surface: Someone sunbathed without a top on, as they had been told to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' suggests sunbathing undressed; it drops the B from BASKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Asked means made a request, inquired.

clue.text: Dead man's chest

parts.note: recalls the pirate song, but a chest here is a box for a corpse

explanation.surface: The pirate shanty about a dead man's treasure chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead man's chest' is a line from the pirate song in Treasure Island; here the chest is the box a body is buried in.
explanation.definitionFit: A box in which a corpse is buried is literally a dead person's chest.

clue.text: Do without and give to others

explanation.surface: Manage without something and share it out instead.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispense with is to forgo, and to dispense also means to hand out or distribute.

clue.text: Each one left spells danger

parts.note: per means each, as in so much per head
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Being the only one left alone is dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spells' is a link meaning makes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Peril is serious danger or risk.

clue.text: Awful rudeness of a number not wearing clothes

indicators.note: awful signals the letters of rudeness are mangled

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: The terrible coarseness of a performance given naked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awful' rearranges RUDENESS into UNDRESSE; 'a number' gives D. 'number' looks like a song or act but is a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Undressed means unclothed, naked.
